{{Short description|Constant in Riemannian geometry}}
{{about|the Cheeger isoperimetric constant and Cheeger's inequality in Riemannian geometry|a different use|Cheeger constant (graph theory)}}

In [[Riemannian geometry]], the '''Cheeger isoperimetric constant''' of a [[compact space|compact]] [[Riemannian manifold]] ''M'' is a positive real number ''h''(''M'') defined in terms of the minimal [[surface area|area]] of a [[hypersurface]] that divides ''M'' into two disjoint pieces. In 1971, [[Jeff Cheeger]] proved an inequality that related the first nontrivial [[eigenvalue]] of the [[Laplace–Beltrami operator]] on ''M'' to ''h''(''M''). In 1982, [[Jürg Peter Buser|Peter Buser]] proved a reverse version of this inequality, and the two inequalities put together are sometimes called the ''Cheeger-Buser inequality''. These inequalities were highly influential not only in Riemannian geometry and [[global analysis]], but also in the theory of [[Markov chain|Markov chains]] and in [[graph theory]], where they have inspired the analogous [[Cheeger constant (graph theory)|Cheeger constant of a graph]] and the notion of [[Conductance (graph theory)|conductance]].

== Definition ==

Let ''M'' be an ''n''-dimensional [[closed manifold|closed]] Riemannian manifold. Let ''V''(''A'') denote the volume of an ''n''-dimensional submanifold ''A'' and ''S''(''E'') denote the ''n''&minus;1-dimensional volume of a submanifold ''E'' (commonly called "area" in this context). The '''Cheeger isoperimetric constant''' of ''M'' is defined to be

: <math> h(M)=\inf_E \frac{S(E)}{\min(V(A), V(B))}, </math>

where the [[infimum]] is taken over all smooth ''n''&minus;1-dimensional submanifolds ''E'' of ''M'' which divide it into two disjoint submanifolds ''A'' and ''B''. The isoperimetric constant may be defined more generally for noncompact Riemannian manifolds of finite volume.

If the manifold is compact with boundary, the infimum is taken over the submanifolds ''E'' which do not intersect the boundary, and the volume of the denominator is that of the disjoint piece whose boundary is only ''E''{{sfn|Cheeger|1971}}. In the non-compact case with infinite volume, the infimum is taken over compact submanifolds ''E'' and the denominator corresponds to the volume of the bounded piece{{sfn|Brooks|1981}}.

== Cheeger's inequality ==

Jeff Cheeger proved{{sfn|Cheeger|1971}} a lower bound for the smallest positive eigenvalue <math>{\lambda_1(M)}</math> of the Laplacian on ''M'' in term of what is now called the Cheeger isoperimetric constant ''h''(''M''):

: <math> \lambda_1(M)\geq \frac{h^2(M)}{4}. </math>

This inequality is optimal in the following sense: for any ''h'' > 0, natural number ''k'', and ''&epsilon;'' > 0, there exists a two-dimensional Riemannian manifold ''M'' with the isoperimetric constant ''h''(''M'') = ''h'' and such that the ''k''th eigenvalue of the Laplacian is within ''&epsilon;'' from the Cheeger bound.{{sfn | Buser | 1978}}

== Buser's inequality ==

[[Jürg Peter Buser|Peter Buser]] proved{{sfn | Buser | 1982}} an upper bound for the smallest positive eigenvalue <math>\lambda_1(M)</math> of the Laplacian on ''M'' in terms of the Cheeger isoperimetric constant ''h''(''M''). Let ''M'' be an ''n''-dimensional closed Riemannian manifold whose [[Ricci curvature]] is bounded below by &minus;(''n''&minus;1)''a''<sup>2</sup>, where ''a'' ≥ 0. Then

: <math> \lambda_1(M)\leq  2a(n-1)h(M) + 10h^2(M).</math>
